## Description

Lagrange interpolation builds a unique polynomial of degree at most $n$ through $n+1$ data points. The animations evaluate it in the first barycentric form, $P_n(x)=\ell(x)\sum_{i=0}^{n} \frac{w_i y_i}{x-x_i}$ with $\ell(x)=\prod_{j=0}^{n}(x-x_j)$ and $w_i=1/\prod_{j\ne i}(x_i-x_j)$. This is the same interpolant, and it stays accurate far outside the nodes, where the second barycentric form (a ratio of two such sums) gives values of the wrong sign in Cases 04 and 29.

Given nodes $(x_i, y_i)$, the interpolation polynomial is

$$
P_n(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{n} y_i L_i(x), \qquad
L_i(x)=\prod_{j\ne i} \frac{x-x_j}{x_i-x_j}.
$$

The 29 animations below follow the legacy Mathews case ordering. Each case heading gives the function and the node interval $[a, b]$; the nodes are equally spaced from $a$ to $b$, endpoints included. Where $f$ is drawn on a wider interval than $[a, b]$ (Cases 04–06, 08–11, 14, 19 and 24–29), the curve beyond the nodes is extrapolation.

## Animations

Each animation raises the polynomial degree through 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13 and 15 (2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 and 16 nodes) for a fixed function and node interval. Where a curve leaves the plot window, it is drawn along the window's top or bottom edge.

[Julia source for all cases](lagnewt_animations_all.jl)

### Case 01: $f(x)=1/(1-x)$, nodes on $[-1.6, 0.9]$

![Lagrange interpolants of f(x) = 1/(1−x) through equally spaced nodes on [−1.6, 0.9], degree rising from 1 to 15, drawn with f on the same interval.](lagnewt01.gif)

### Case 12: $f(x)=\sin x$, nodes on $[-3\pi, 3\pi]$

With 2, 3 and 4 nodes every node is a multiple of $\pi$, where $\sin x = 0$, so the frames titled degree 1, 2 and 3 all show the line $y = 0$.

![Lagrange interpolants of f(x) = sin x through equally spaced nodes on [−3π, 3π], degree rising from 1 to 15, drawn with f on the same interval; at degrees 1, 2 and 3 every node is a multiple of π, so the interpolant is the line y = 0.](lagnewt12.gif)

### Case 13: $f(x)=\cos x$, nodes on $[-3\pi, 3\pi]$

With 2 and 4 nodes every node is an odd multiple of $\pi$, where $\cos x = -1$, so the frames titled degree 1 and 3 show the line $y = -1$.

![Lagrange interpolants of f(x) = cos x through equally spaced nodes on [−3π, 3π], degree rising from 1 to 15, drawn with f on the same interval; at degrees 1 and 3 every node is an odd multiple of π, so the interpolant is the line y = −1.](lagnewt13.gif)
